findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: nextIntUnbiased(n) is exactly uniform for every n in 1..2^31, as its doc comment and the spec interface say. Actual: for large non-power-of-two n, the double product u*n goes over 2^53 and the low word is rounded, so the accept/reject decision can be wrong. Example: n = 2^31-1 and a raw draw of 4294967294. The exact low word is above the threshold (3), so the exact result is 2147483646 on the first draw. The method instead rejects that draw, makes a second nextUint32 call and returns a different value. The deck (n <= 52) is unaffected, and the builder followed spec rule 3 literally.
findings.fix: Either document and enforce the exact range as n <= 2^21 (the spec interface comment needs updating too), or compute the 64-bit product exactly (e.g. split the 32-bit draw into 16-bit halves) so that every n up to 2^31 is exact.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: if the shuffle used the biased nextInt instead of nextIntUnbiased, at least one test would fail. Actual: with that change all deck, acceptance and seeded-random tests still pass, because none of the golden or property codes hits a rejection (the chance is about 3e-7 per deck). The production code is correct; this is a test-strength gap.
findings.fix: Add a deck golden vector for a replay code whose shuffle hits a rejection in nextIntUnbiased (found by search), or assert that shuffledDeck uses the unbiased draw through a code known to trigger rejection.
